# Course-end exit oracle (2026-10-24, changes/2026-10-24-lane-clearance/; NORMATIVE for the switch).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
COURSE_END_TOL = 1e-9


def check_course_end_oracle(verbose: bool = True) -> float:
    """k0_mean = 3 leftovers, no introductions, spread, clearance or detection, course-end exit ON (the
    nws within-premises course: latent 2 d, doubling 3.6 d, recovery 7 d, N_herd 100, seed 1 animal).
    A leftover at grid age j*dt leaves when j + n reaches i_end (n steps elapsed), so with the initial
    weights w_j of the lane's own grid law P_free(n dt) = exp(-3 sum_{j < i_end - n} w_j): fresh
    leftovers give e^{-3} before tau_end and 1 after; aged ones (age0_scale 14) the thinned curve."""
    base = dict(k0_mean=3.0, mean_intro_interval=float("inf"), doubling_time=float("inf"),
                Se_animal=0.0, rho_r=0.0, rho_a=0.0, horizon=180.0,
                round_times=(30.0, 60.0, 90.0, 120.0, 150.0, 160.0, 170.0, 180.0), course_end_exit=True,
                mean_latent_time=2.0, doubling_time_within=3.6, mean_recovery_time_within=7.0,
                N_herd=100, p_latent_seed=0.01, p_infectious_seed=0.0)
    h = float(DEFAULTS["dt"])
    nT = int(round(180.0 / h))
    worst = 0.0
    for a0 in (0.0, 14.0):
        out = evaluate(dict(base, age0_scale=a0))
        i_end = int(round(out["_tau_end"] / h))
        w = np.exp(-rate_from_mean(a0) * np.arange(nT + 1) * h)
        w = w / w.sum()
        for t in sorted(out["p_free_by_time"]):
            n = int(round(t / h))
            # t = 0 is the initial state (every leftover counted, e^{-3}); from the first step on, the
            # leftovers already at or past tau_end have left
            expect = math.exp(-3.0) if n == 0 else math.exp(-3.0 * float(w[:max(i_end - n, 0)].sum()))
            got = out["p_free_by_time"][t]
            worst = max(worst, abs(got - expect))
            if verbose:
                print(f"   age0_scale={a0:4.0f} tau_end={out['_tau_end']:.2f}  t={t:5.0f}  P_free={got:.12f}"
                      f"  grid law={expect:.12f}  |diff|={abs(got - expect):.1e}")
            assert abs(got - expect) < COURSE_END_TOL, f"course-end oracle broken at age0 {a0}, t {t}"
    return worst


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Rate-schedule self-test (2026-11-18, model_design.md "Rate schedule"; NORMATIVE for this lane).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEDULE_ORACLE_TOL = 1e-9              # closed form vs exp(-lambda_region * A(t))
SCHEDULE_EQUIV_TOL = 1e-12              # a schedule vs the equivalent unscheduled parameter


def _identical(a, b) -> bool:
    """Exact equality of two evaluate() outputs: same keys in the same order, same types, and every
    value equal under == (no tolerance)."""
    if isinstance(a, dict):
        return (isinstance(b, dict) and list(a.keys()) == list(b.keys())
                and all(_identical(a[k], b[k]) for k in a))
    if isinstance(a, (list, tuple)):
        return type(a) is type(b) and len(a) == len(b) and all(_identical(x, y) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    return type(a) is type(b) and a == b


def check_rate_schedule(verbose: bool = True) -> dict:
    """NORMATIVE (2026-11-18). (a) Unit multipliers: a schedule whose multipliers are all 1, at
    breakpoints that fall inside and between rounds, returns every output of the unscheduled run
    exactly (==), on the lane defaults and on the six_months and early_warning presets. (b) Oracle:
    no detection, spread, exits or initial premises, three segments (multipliers 1, 0, 2.5 from 0,
    60 and 120 d): P_free(t) = exp(-lambda_region * A(t)), A the integral of the introduction
    multiplier, to 1e-9, flat across the zero segment. (c) spread_multiplier = 0 in every segment
    equals doubling_time = Inf on every P_free to 1e-12, with P_R_gt0 = 0. (d) An introduction
    multiplier of c in every segment equals mean_intro_interval / c with no schedule, to 1e-12.
    (e) Each malformed schedule the spec lists raises ValueError."""
    presets = _load_presets()
    h = float(DEFAULTS["dt"])
    six = presets.preset_to_params(presets.SCENARIOS["six_months"], h)
    assert all(six.get(k) is None for k in SCHEDULE_KEYS), \
        "six_months now carries a rate schedule of its own; checks (c) and (d) need an unscheduled preset"
    worst = {}

    # (a) unit multipliers, exact
    cases = [("lane defaults", {}), ("six_months", six),
             ("early_warning", presets.preset_to_params(presets.SCENARIOS["early_warning"], h))]
    for name, p in cases:
        assert all(p.get(k) is None for k in SCHEDULE_KEYS), \
            f"{name} now carries a rate schedule of its own; pick an unscheduled preset for check (a)"
        hz = float(p.get("horizon", DEFAULTS["horizon"]))
        ones = dict(schedule_times=[0.0, 10.05, 30.0, hz - h], intro_multiplier=[1.0] * 4,
                    spread_multiplier=[1.0] * 4)
        same = _identical(evaluate(p), evaluate(dict(p, **ones)))
        if verbose:
            print(f"   (a) unit multipliers, {name:<14} every output == the unscheduled run: {same}")
        assert same, f"{name}: a schedule of unit multipliers changed an output"

    # (b) oracle: P(K = 0)(t) = exp(-lambda_region * A(t))
    interval, sched_t, a = 130.0, [0.0, 60.0, 120.0], [1.0, 0.0, 2.5]
    out = evaluate(dict(
        mean_intro_interval=interval, Se_animal=0.0, rho_r=0.0, rho_a=0.0,
        doubling_time=float("inf"), mean_recovery_time=float("inf"), course_end_exit=False,
        k0_mean=0.0, horizon=180.0, round_times=(30.0, 60.0, 90.0, 120.0, 150.0, 180.0),
        eval_times=[0.0, 45.0, 60.05, 75.0, 119.95, 120.05, 165.0],
        schedule_times=sched_t, intro_multiplier=a, spread_multiplier=[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]))

    def A(t):
        ends = sched_t[1:] + [float("inf")]
        return sum(aj * max(0.0, min(t, e) - s0) for aj, s0, e in zip(a, sched_t, ends))

    worst["oracle"] = 0.0
    for t in sorted(out["p_free_by_time"]):
        expect = math.exp(-A(t) / interval)
        got = out["p_free_by_time"][t]
        worst["oracle"] = max(worst["oracle"], abs(got - expect))
        if verbose:
            print(f"   (b) t={t:7.2f}  A(t)={A(t):7.2f}  P_free={got:.14f}  exp(-lam A)={expect:.14f}"
                  f"  |diff|={abs(got - expect):.1e}")
        assert abs(got - expect) < SCHEDULE_ORACLE_TOL, \
            f"rate-schedule oracle broken at t={t}: got {got!r}, expected {expect!r}"
    # Cumulative incidence under the same schedule: each of the M premises is infested at rate
    # a(t) * lambda_region / M and never leaves, so E[K(t)] = M (1 - exp(-lambda_region A(t) / M)).
    # The lane's incidence is a left-endpoint sum over the steps (first order in dt), hence 1e-3.
    Mz = int(DEFAULTS["M"])
    ci_expect = Mz * (1.0 - math.exp(-A(180.0) / interval / Mz))
    worst["oracle_incidence"] = abs(out["cumulative_incidence"] - ci_expect)
    if verbose:
        print(f"   (b) cumulative incidence={out['cumulative_incidence']:.6f}  "
              f"M (1 - exp(-lam A / M))={ci_expect:.6f}  |diff|={worst['oracle_incidence']:.1e}")
    assert worst["oracle_incidence"] < 1e-3, "rate-schedule oracle: cumulative incidence off the scheduled law"

    # (c) no spread by schedule == no spread by parameter
    zero = evaluate(dict(six, schedule_times=[0.0, 45.0], intro_multiplier=[1.0, 1.0],
                         spread_multiplier=[0.0, 0.0]))
    noss = evaluate(dict(six, doubling_time=float("inf")))
    worst["spread_zero"] = max(abs(zero["p_free_by_time"][t] - noss["p_free_by_time"][t])
                               for t in noss["p_free_by_time"])
    worst["spread_zero_R"] = abs(zero["P_R_gt0"])
    if verbose:
        print(f"   (c) spread_multiplier = 0 vs doubling_time = Inf on six_months: max|dP_free| = "
              f"{worst['spread_zero']:.1e}, P_R_gt0 = {zero['P_R_gt0']:.1e} (parameter route "
              f"{noss['P_R_gt0']:.1e})")
    assert worst["spread_zero"] < SCHEDULE_EQUIV_TOL, "spread_multiplier = 0 differs from doubling_time = Inf"
    assert worst["spread_zero_R"] < SCHEDULE_EQUIV_TOL, "spread_multiplier = 0 left secondary spread"

    # (d) a constant introduction multiplier == the scaled interval
    c = 2.5
    sc = evaluate(dict(six, schedule_times=[0.0, 30.0, 95.0], intro_multiplier=[c] * 3,
                       spread_multiplier=[1.0] * 3))
    un = evaluate(dict(six, mean_intro_interval=float(six["mean_intro_interval"]) / c))
    worst["intro_const"] = max(
        max(abs(sc["p_free_by_time"][t] - un["p_free_by_time"][t]) for t in un["p_free_by_time"]),
        max(abs(sc[k] - un[k]) for k in ("P_lost_freedom", "cumulative_incidence", "P_R_gt0")))
    if verbose:
        print(f"   (d) intro_multiplier = {c} throughout vs mean_intro_interval / {c} on six_months: "
              f"max|d| over P_free, P_lost_freedom, cumulative_incidence, P_R_gt0 = {worst['intro_const']:.1e}")
    assert worst["intro_const"] < SCHEDULE_EQUIV_TOL, "constant intro_multiplier differs from the scaled interval"

    # (e) malformed schedules
    ok = dict(schedule_times=[0.0, 30.0], intro_multiplier=[1.0, 2.0], spread_multiplier=[1.0, 0.5])
    bad = {
        "times without multipliers": dict(schedule_times=[0.0, 30.0]),
        "one multiplier list missing": dict(ok, spread_multiplier=None),
        "unequal lengths": dict(ok, intro_multiplier=[1.0]),
        "first breakpoint not 0": dict(ok, schedule_times=[5.0, 30.0]),
        "breakpoints not increasing": dict(ok, schedule_times=[0.0, 0.0]),
        "negative multiplier": dict(ok, intro_multiplier=[1.0, -0.1]),
        "non-finite multiplier": dict(ok, spread_multiplier=[1.0, float("inf")]),
        "NaN multiplier": dict(ok, intro_multiplier=[float("nan"), 1.0]),
        "breakpoint off the dt grid": dict(ok, schedule_times=[0.0, 30.02]),
        "empty lists": dict(schedule_times=[], intro_multiplier=[], spread_multiplier=[]),
    }
    for label, over in bad.items():
        try:
            evaluate(over)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        raise AssertionError(f"malformed rate schedule accepted: {label}")
    if verbose:
        print(f"   (e) {len(bad)} malformed schedules each raise ValueError")
    return worst


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("=== self-test / smoke run (closed-form lane) ===\n")

    # (1) Flagship FMD baseline (validation scenario).
    base = evaluate({})
    print("FMD baseline P_free by round time:")
    for t in sorted(base["p_free_by_time"]):
        print(f"   t={t:6.1f} d  P_free={base['p_free_by_time'][t]:.4f}")
    print(f"   P_lost_freedom={base['P_lost_freedom']:.4f}  cum_incidence={base['cumulative_incidence']:.4f}")
    print(f"   P_R_gt0={base['P_R_gt0']:.4f}  expected_cost={base['expected_cost']:.2f}"
          f"  cost/farm={base['cost_share_per_farm']:.4f}\n")

    # (2) ORACLE: no introductions -> P_free == 1 at all times.
    o1 = evaluate({"mean_intro_interval": float("inf")})
    m1 = max(abs(v - 1.0) for v in o1["p_free_by_time"].values())
    print(f"[oracle] no-intro  max|P_free-1| = {m1:.2e}  (expect ~0)")

    # (3) ORACLE: no detection (Se=0, rho_r=0, no spread) -> P_free == P(K=0) == exp(-lam t).
    o2 = evaluate({"Se_animal": 0.0, "rho_r": 0.0, "doubling_time": float("inf")})
    lam = 1.0 / 50.0
    worst = 0.0
    for t, v in o2["p_free_by_time"].items():
        if t == 0:
            continue
        worst = max(worst, abs(v - math.exp(-lam * t)))
    print(f"[oracle] no-detect max|P_free-exp(-lam t)| = {worst:.2e}  (expect small)")

    # (4) CONTINUITY GATE: latent=0 vs latent=1e-6 must agree (inverted-limit detector).
    z0 = evaluate({"mean_latent_time": 0.0})
    ze = evaluate({"mean_latent_time": 1e-6})
    cont = max(abs(z0["p_free_by_time"][t] - ze["p_free_by_time"][t]) for t in z0["p_free_by_time"])
    ag = np.arange(int(round(120 / 0.5)) + 1) * 0.5
    ps0 = within_farm_curves(dict(DEFAULTS, mean_latent_time=0.0), ag)["p_shed"]
    pse = within_farm_curves(dict(DEFAULTS, mean_latent_time=1e-6), ag)["p_shed"]
    print(f"[continuity] latent 0 vs 1e-6: max|dP_free|={cont:.2e}, "
          f"max|dp_shed|={np.max(np.abs(ps0 - pse)):.2e}  (expect ~0)")
    print(f"             p_shed(latent=0) at tau=30d = {ps0[60]:.3f}  (should be large, NOT ~0.01)")

    # (5) EVIDENCE-STRENGTH MONOTONICITY.
    #
    # Two different quantities move in opposite directions with more testing:
    #
    #   P_free  = P(K <= K* | NO ALARM)  -- conditional. RISES with more testing, because
    #             surviving a more searching test is stronger evidence of freedom.
    #   _P_D0   = P(no alarm)            -- unconditional. FALLS with more testing, because
    #             a harder test is harder to pass.
    #
    # Both are correct simultaneously; they answer different questions. Both are asserted.
    assert_monotonicity()
    print("[monotone] P_free rises and P(no alarm) falls with more testing (both asserted)")

    # ---- v0.6-nws pre-seeded start ---------------------------------------------------
    # (6) REDUCTION ANCHOR (normative, model_design.md "Degenerate limits"): at k0_mean = 0
    #     the lane must reproduce the 2026-09-08 closed-form smoke run to machine precision.
    #     19 named cells, each row carrying every parameter and its own 180-d schedule. The
    #     two cells with a doubling time under 0.25 d carry expected values regenerated on
    #     2026-11-19 at the shared 0.1 d floor (the other 17 are the 2026-09-08 values).
    print(f"\n[reduction anchor] k0_mean = 0 vs the 2026-09-08 lane, tol {ANCHOR_TOL:.0e}:")
    worst_anchor = check_reduction_anchors()
    print(f"   max |P_free - expected| over the anchor cells = {worst_anchor:.2e}  (asserted < {ANCHOR_TOL:.0e})")

    # (7) POISSON-THINNING ORACLE (normative, validation_design.md `oracle_poisson_thinning`):
    #     P_free(t) = exp(-3 e^{-t/21}) at every round, e^{-3} at t = 0, t_release from it.
    print(f"\n[oracle] Poisson thinning (k0_mean=3, all fresh, no intro/spread/detection, "
          f"clearance 21 d), tol {ORACLE_TOL:.0e}:")
    worst_oracle = check_poisson_thinning_oracle()
    print(f"   max |P_free - exp(-3 e^(-t/21))| = {worst_oracle:.2e}  (asserted < {ORACLE_TOL:.0e})")

    # (8) CONTINUITY GATES at the new degenerate boundaries (memory.md: f(0) ~ f(eps)).
    #     k0_mean 0 vs 1e-9: the initial cohort's whole effect is O(1e-9), so the reduction is
    #     the limit, not a special case. age0_scale 0 vs 1e-6 (at k0_mean = 2): both floor to
    #     the same time-scale, so the two runs must coincide.
    c0 = evaluate({"k0_mean": 0.0})
    ce = evaluate({"k0_mean": 1e-9})
    d_k0 = max(abs(c0["p_free_by_time"][t] - ce["p_free_by_time"][t]) for t in c0["p_free_by_time"])
    a0 = evaluate({"k0_mean": 2.0, "age0_scale": 0.0})
    ae = evaluate({"k0_mean": 2.0, "age0_scale": 1e-6})
    d_a0 = max(abs(a0["p_free_by_time"][t] - ae["p_free_by_time"][t]) for t in a0["p_free_by_time"])
    print(f"\n[continuity] k0_mean 0 vs 1e-9: max|dP_free|={d_k0:.2e} (expect ~1e-9); "
          f"age0_scale 0 vs 1e-6 at k0_mean=2: max|dP_free|={d_a0:.2e} (expect 0)")
    assert d_k0 < 1e-6, f"k0_mean boundary is not continuous: {d_k0}"
    assert d_a0 < 1e-9, f"age0_scale boundary is not continuous: {d_a0}"

    # (8b) SHARED DOUBLING FLOOR (model_design.md "Shared floors"): a doubling time at or below
    #      0.1 d is evaluated at 0.1 d, so 0.1, 0.0999, 0.05 and 0 give the same outputs exactly,
    #      for both doubling times; and 0.2 d is above the floor, so it is evaluated as written
    #      and differs from 0.1 d.
    assert MIN_TIMESCALE == 1e-3 and MIN_DOUBLING == 0.1, "the shared floors are 1e-3 d and 0.1 d"
    for key in ("doubling_time_within", "doubling_time"):
        at = evaluate({key: MIN_DOUBLING})
        for below in (0.0999, 0.05, 0.0):
            lo = evaluate({key: below})
            assert _identical(at, lo), f"{key} = {below} differs from {key} = {MIN_DOUBLING} (the floor)"
        above = evaluate({key: 0.2})
        d_fl = max(abs(at["p_free_by_time"][t] - above["p_free_by_time"][t]) for t in at["p_free_by_time"])
        assert d_fl > 1e-9, f"{key} = 0.2 d is above the floor but equals the floored run"
        print(f"[floor] {key}: 0.1, 0.0999, 0.05 and 0 d identical (asserted); "
              f"0.2 d evaluated as written, max|dP_free| vs 0.1 d = {d_fl:.2e}")

    # (9) EVIDENCE-STRENGTH MONOTONICITY with initial premises present (k0_mean = 2,
    #     age0_scale = 14): the same three sweeps as (5) on the pre-seeded start.
    assert_monotonicity(k0_mean=2.0, age0_scale=14.0)
    print("[monotone] ... and with initial premises present (k0_mean=2, age0_scale=14; asserted)")

    # (10) THE RELEASE TRANSIENT on the reviewed screwworm backdrop (anchor row 0: the OAT
    #      star centre, 6 monthly rounds to 180 d) with the zone-preset placeholders
    #      k0_mean = 1, age0_scale = 14 (priors_design.md): P_free starts at e^{-1} and climbs;
    #      t_release reads off the crossing. Then the age0_scale direction (scenarios.md #18,
    #      asserted there, REPORTED here): P_free at a fixed t vs the leftovers' mean age.
    backdrop = load_anchor_cells()[0]["params"]
    zone = evaluate(dict(backdrop, k0_mean=1.0, age0_scale=14.0))
    print("\n[transient] reviewed backdrop + k0_mean=1, age0_scale=14 (zone-preset placeholders):")
    for t in sorted(zone["p_free_by_time"]):
        print(f"   t={t:6.1f} d  P_free={zone['p_free_by_time'][t]:.6f}")
    print(f"   t_release={zone['t_release']} at threshold {zone['release_threshold']};  "
          f"P_lost_freedom={zone['P_lost_freedom']:.4f}  cum_incidence={zone['cumulative_incidence']:.4f}"
          f"  P_R_gt0={zone['P_R_gt0']:.4f}")
    assert abs(zone["p_free_by_time"][0.0] - math.exp(-1.0)) < 1e-12, "P_free(0) != e^{-k0_mean}"
    print("   P_free(0) = e^{-1} to 1e-12 (asserted; truncation at M=100 is far below that)")
    ages = [0.0, 3.0, 14.0, 60.0, 180.0]
    marks = [30.0, 90.0, 180.0]
    rows = []
    for a in ages:
        o = evaluate(dict(backdrop, k0_mean=2.0, age0_scale=a))
        rows.append([o["p_free_by_time"][t] for t in marks])
        print(f"   k0_mean=2, age0_scale={a:5.0f}: " +
              "  ".join(f"P_free({t:.0f})={v:.6f}" for t, v in zip(marks, rows[-1])) +
              f"  t_release={o['t_release']}")
    for j, t in enumerate(marks):
        col = [r[j] for r in rows]
        mono = all(col[i] >= col[i - 1] - 1e-9 for i in range(1, len(col)))
        print(f"   P_free({t:.0f}) non-decreasing in age0_scale: {'yes' if mono else 'NO'}"
              f"  (scenarios.md #18, reported not asserted)")

    # (11) EVALUATION TIMES (2026-09-15, changes/2026-09-09-eval-times, normative): a pure addition.
    #      (a) round values and scalars identical to the plain run on the five screwworm presets,
    #      (b) interior values equal truncated re-evaluation at a clean start, (c) the aged-start
    #      difference is the documented one (higher early, same from 45 d).
    print(f"\n[eval times] pure addition, tol round/scalar {EVAL_ROUND_TOL:.0e}, interior {EVAL_INTERIOR_TOL:.0e}, "
          f"aged from 45 d {EVAL_AGED_TOL:.0e}:")
    w = check_eval_times()
    print(f"   worst: round {w['round']:.1e}, scalar {w['scalar']:.1e}, interior {w['interior']:.1e}, "
          f"from 45 d {w['aged_late']:.1e}  (all asserted)")

    # (12) COURSE-END EXIT ORACLE (2026-10-24): leftovers leave at tau_end, nothing else happens.
    print(f"\n[oracle] course-end exit (k0_mean=3, nothing else), tol {COURSE_END_TOL:.0e}:")
    w = check_course_end_oracle()
    print(f"   max |P_free - grid law| = {w:.1e}  (asserted)")

    # (13) RATE SCHEDULE (2026-11-18, normative): unit multipliers change nothing (exact), the
    #      exp(-lambda A(t)) oracle on three segments, spread multiplier 0 against doubling time Inf,
    #      a constant introduction multiplier against the scaled interval, and the input errors.
    print(f"\n[rate schedule] unit multipliers exact, oracle tol {SCHEDULE_ORACLE_TOL:.0e}, "
          f"equivalences tol {SCHEDULE_EQUIV_TOL:.0e}:")
    w = check_rate_schedule()
    print(f"   worst: oracle {w['oracle']:.1e}, spread 0 vs Inf {w['spread_zero']:.1e}, "
          f"constant intro {w['intro_const']:.1e}  (all asserted)")

    print("\nall invariants passed.")

name: nearby_index.py
content:
"""Nearby-pressure index: turns the official confirmed detections into the `nearby_pressure`
input of the introduction module (intro_design.md, "Nearby detections" and "Linked counties").

For a county and a date the raw value is a sum over confirmed animal cases in OTHER counties in the
30 days up to that date. Each case counts kernel(distance) * south_weight(direction), with the
distance and direction measured between county internal points. The index is the raw value divided
by its reference level: the mean raw value over the county-days that produced the reference
introduction rate (counties with no case of their own that adjoin a county with a case, 13 June to
5 September 2026; priors_design.md, `mean_intro_interval`). So the index is 1, on average, under the
conditions in which the reference rate was counted.

Pure Python (csv, math, datetime only) and no network, so it can run in the browser build of the app.
The data come from CSV files in the repository; the default paths are below.
Numbers and checks: changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/README.md.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import math
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

_EX = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
CASES_CSV = _EX / "changes/2026-11-18-county-tailoring/data/detections_official.csv"
CENTROIDS_CSV = _EX / "changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/data/county_centroids_all.csv"
ADJACENCY_CSV = _EX / "changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/data/county_adjacency.csv"

# Defaults and the ranges to explore. Both dials have thin data behind them (see intro_design.md).
DEFAULTS = dict(
    kernel_km=150.0,         # distance scale of the kernel, km: the historical seasonal front moved
                             # 80 to 160 km per fly generation, about 100 to 200 km per 30 days
    south_weight=2.0,        # weight of a case in a county due south, relative to due north (1 = none)
    kernel_shape="power",    # "power": 1 / (1 + (d / L)^2); "exponential": exp(-d / L)
    window_days=30,          # cases confirmed in the 30 days up to the date
)
RANGES = dict(kernel_km=(30.0, 300.0), south_weight=(1.0, 5.0))
# The period and the county set behind the reference introduction rate (priors_design.md): 85 days
# after 12 June 2026, counties with no case so far that adjoin a county with a case.
REF_START = date(2026, 6, 13)
REF_END = date(2026, 9, 5)
MONTH_DAYS = 30.0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- data loading
def load_cases(path=CASES_CSV) -> list:
    """Confirmed animal cases as (date, (state, county)); fly-trap detections are left out."""
    out = []
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            if r["case_type"] == "Fly Trap":
                continue
            out.append((date.fromisoformat(r["confirmed_date"]), (r["state"], r["county"])))
    return sorted(out)


def load_centroids(path=CENTROIDS_CSV) -> dict:
    """County internal points: {(state, county): (lat, lon)}."""
    out = {}
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            out[(r["state"], r["county"])] = (float(r["lat"]), float(r["lon"]))
    return out


def load_adjacency(path=ADJACENCY_CSV, centroids_path=CENTROIDS_CSV) -> dict:
    """County adjacency as {(state, county): set of (state, county)}. Neighbours outside the three
    states of the centroid file are dropped."""
    key = {}
    with open(centroids_path, newline="") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            key[r["geoid"]] = (r["state"], r["county"])
    out = {}
    with open(path, newline="") as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            if r["geoid"] in key and r["neighbor_geoid"] in key:
                out.setdefault(key[r["geoid"]], set()).add(key[r["neighbor_geoid"]])
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- geometry and weights
def distance_km(a: tuple, b: tuple) -> float:
    """Great-circle distance between two (lat, lon) points."""
    p1, l1, p2, l2 = map(math.radians, (a[0], a[1], b[0], b[1]))
    x = math.sin((p2 - p1) / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin((l2 - l1) / 2) ** 2
    return 6371.0 * 2 * math.asin(math.sqrt(x))


def southness(target: tuple, source: tuple) -> float:
    """How far south of the target the source lies, 0 to 1: the cosine of the angle between the
    direction to the source and due south, and 0 when the source is not south of the target."""
    p1, p2 = math.radians(target[0]), math.radians(source[0])
    dl = math.radians(source[1] - target[1])
    y = math.sin(dl) * math.cos(p2)
    x = math.cos(p1) * math.sin(p2) - math.sin(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.cos(dl)
    bearing = math.atan2(y, x)                 # 0 = north, pi = south
    return max(0.0, -math.cos(bearing))


def kernel(d_km: float, kernel_km: float, shape: str = "power") -> float:
    if shape == "power":
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + (d_km / kernel_km) ** 2)
    if shape == "exponential":
        return math.exp(-d_km / kernel_km)
    raise ValueError("kernel_shape must be 'power' or 'exponential'")


def pair_weight(target: tuple, source: tuple, kernel_km=DEFAULTS["kernel_km"],
                south_weight=DEFAULTS["south_weight"], kernel_shape=DEFAULTS["kernel_shape"]) -> float:
    """Weight of one case at `source` for a county at `target` (both (lat, lon))."""
    return (kernel(distance_km(target, source), kernel_km, kernel_shape)
            * (1.0 + (south_weight - 1.0) * southness(target, source)))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- the index
def raw_index(county: tuple, on: date, cases: list, centroids: dict, exclude=(), **dials) -> float:
    """Weighted count of cases in other counties confirmed in the window ending on `on` (inclusive).
    `exclude` lists further counties to leave out (the members of a linked group, whose pressure
    comes from the model instead)."""
    d = dict(DEFAULTS, **dials)
    start = on - timedelta(days=int(d["window_days"]))
    skip = {county, *exclude}
    here = centroids[county]
    total, cache = 0.0, {}
    for when, src in cases:
        if when <= start or when > on or src in skip:
            continue
        if src not in cache:
            cache[src] = pair_weight(here, centroids[src], d["kernel_km"], d["south_weight"],
                                     d["kernel_shape"])
        total += cache[src]
    return total


def index_breakdown(county: tuple, on: date, cases: list, centroids: dict, reference: float = 1.0,
                    exclude=(), **dials) -> list:
    """The index split by source county, largest first: one dict per county with cases in the window
    (cases, km, southness, weight per case, contribution). The contributions sum to the index."""
    d = dict(DEFAULTS, **dials)
    start = on - timedelta(days=int(d["window_days"]))
    skip = {county, *exclude}
    here = centroids[county]
    n = {}
    for when, src in cases:
        if start < when <= on and src not in skip:
            n[src] = n.get(src, 0) + 1
    rows = []
    for src, k in n.items():
        w = pair_weight(here, centroids[src], d["kernel_km"], d["south_weight"], d["kernel_shape"])
        rows.append(dict(state=src[0], county=src[1], cases=k,
                         km=distance_km(here, centroids[src]), southness=southness(here, centroids[src]),
                         weight_per_case=w / reference, contribution=k * w / reference))
    return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r["contribution"])


def at_risk_counties(on: date, cases: list, adjacency: dict) -> list:
    """Counties with no case up to `on` that adjoin a county with a case up to `on`."""
    hit = {src for when, src in cases if when <= on}
    return sorted(c for c, nb in adjacency.items() if c not in hit and nb & hit)


def reference_level(cases: list, centroids: dict, adjacency: dict, start: date = REF_START,
                    end: date = REF_END, **dials) -> dict:
    """Mean raw index over the at-risk county-days of the reference period, with the counts behind
    it: county-days, the daily number of at-risk counties, and the first detections that fell on an
    at-risk county (the events the reference rate counted)."""
    first = {}
    for when, src in cases:
        first.setdefault(src, when)
    total, n, per_day, events = 0.0, 0, [], []
    day = start
    while day <= end:
        risk = at_risk_counties(day - timedelta(days=1), cases, adjacency)
        per_day.append(len(risk))
        for c in risk:
            total += raw_index(c, day, cases, centroids, **dials)
            n += 1
            if first.get(c) == day:
                events.append((day.isoformat(), c[1]))
        day += timedelta(days=1)
    return dict(level=total / n, county_days=n, at_risk_min=min(per_day), at_risk_max=max(per_day),
                at_risk_mean=n / len(per_day), days=len(per_day), events=events)


def nearby_index(county: tuple, on: date, cases: list, centroids: dict, reference: float,
                 exclude=(), **dials) -> float:
    """The index for `county` on a date: raw value over the reference level (same dials for both)."""
    return raw_index(county, on, cases, centroids, exclude=exclude, **dials) / reference


def index_by_segment(county: tuple, start: date, n_segments: int, cases: list, centroids: dict,
                     reference: float, data_end: date | None = None, exclude=(), **dials) -> list:
    """One index value per 30-day segment of a run that starts on `start`. Each segment uses the
    cases known when it begins (the 30 days up to its first day), so nothing looks ahead. Segments
    that begin after `data_end` (default: the last case date) keep the value at `data_end`."""
    data_end = data_end or max(when for when, _ in cases)
    out = []
    for j in range(n_segments):
        on = min(start + timedelta(days=int(MONTH_DAYS) * j), data_end)
        out.append(nearby_index(county, on, cases, centroids, reference, exclude=exclude, **dials))
    return out


def schedule_with_index(intro_module, m: dict, horizon_days: float, nearby: list,
                        wildlife_follows_index: bool = False) -> dict:
    """The rate schedule of intro_module.schedule with `nearby_pressure` set segment by segment.
    `nearby` has one value per 30-day segment; a list of equal values reproduces
    intro_module.schedule. With `wildlife_follows_index` the wildlife share is scaled by the index
    too (an option examined in the 2026 check; off by default, as in the module)."""
    n_seg = max(1, int(math.ceil(float(horizon_days) / MONTH_DAYS - 1e-9)))
    if len(nearby) < n_seg:
        raise ValueError("need one nearby value per 30-day segment")
    start = int(m["start_month"]) - 1
    shift = float(m.get("temp_shift", 0.0))
    season_on = bool(m.get("season_on", True))
    times, intro, spread, rows = [], [], [], []
    for j in range(n_seg):
        k = (start + j) % 12
        act = (intro_module.season_activity(m["monthly_tmax"][k] + shift, m["monthly_tmin"][k] + shift)
               if season_on else 1.0)
        mj = dict(m, nearby_pressure=float(nearby[j]))
        pw = intro_module.pathway_rates(mj, act)
        wild = pw["wild"] * (max(0.0, float(nearby[j])) if wildlife_follows_index else 1.0)
        a = pw["fly"] + pw["move"] + wild
        s = intro_module.spread_multiplier(mj, act)
        times.append(j * MONTH_DAYS)
        intro.append(a)
        spread.append(s)
        rows.append(dict(month=intro_module.MONTH_NAMES[k], activity=act, nearby=float(nearby[j]),
                         fly=pw["fly"], move=pw["move"], wild=wild, intro=a, spread=s))
    return dict(schedule_times=times, intro_multiplier=intro, spread_multiplier=spread, rows=rows)

"""Scenario presets for the nws-freedom review app: the ONE table the app, the stage-5 scenario
runner (and any future video data pass) all read, so they cannot drift.

Every entry carries a COMPLETE input set (keys are app input ids, not model parameter names), so
loading one leaves nothing behind from the previous scenario. `preset_to_params()` is the single
mapping from app inputs to the lane's parameter dict; app.py uses it for its sliders and the
scenario runner uses it for the presets.

Priors: priors_design.md, first-pass literature review folded 2026-09-08 (within doubling 4.5 d,
within recovery 7 d, f_clinical_max 0.9, rho_r 0.33 /d; zone rows per cluster C). Decisions F1 (the
four screwworm presets), A8 (default horizon 180 d, marks 30/60/90/120/180), C11 (clearance on).

v0.6 (pre-seeded start, 2026-09-09): every pack carries the initial state `k0_mean` / `age0_scale`,
the four zone presets start with leftovers (1 premises, mean age 14 d, both guessed), the clean start
stays the default so the scenario-check presets are the reduction anchor (scenarios.md #16), and
`preset_to_params()` passes the initial state and `release_threshold` through to the lane.

2026-10-23 (parameter-pack correction, accepted 2026-10-23, changes/2026-10-24-clearance-and-doubling/):
(1) zone clearance OFF in the default pack (`clearance_on=False`, so `mean_recovery_time = Inf`): on
the freedom path every premises still counted is undetected, and the 21-d clearance came from the
release rule for detected, treated premises. The 21 d stays as the slider value for when the box is
ticked. Scenario-check presets whose scenarios.md entry says "clearance on" now say so explicitly, and
`six_months_clear` is the clearance-on twin for checks 4 and 9. (2) `doubling_time_within` 4.5 to
3.6 d, re-derived with the model's own within-premises recovery time (7 d) instead of about 14 d.

2026-10-24 (lane change, accepted 2026-10-28, changes/2026-10-24-lane-clearance/): (1) `course_end_on`
(lane `course_end_exit`): an undetected premises leaves the count when its own within-premises course
has run out (fewer than half an animal still infested); (2) `release_on` / `release_mean` (lane
`mean_release_time`): after a detection (D = 1) counted premises clear on the 21-d release clock, as
treated premises do. Both ON in this pack; both OFF at the lane defaults, so regional-freedom and any
pack without them is unchanged. The analytic-oracle presets (checks 2, 3, 4 no-detection pair, 14) set
`course_end_on=False` explicitly: their textbook formulas are for the chain without the exit, and the
exit has its own oracle check (19).
"""

def renewed_rate(pack: dict) -> float:
    """Added introduction rate per day for the what-if term on renewed infestations.

    The check against 2026 found more renewed detections in counties with an earlier case than the
    model gives, and the model has no term for it. The cause is not known. This what-if enters a
    chance p per 30 days as a constant rate h = -ln(1 - p) / 30 per day. It is not scaled by the
    season, sterile-fly coverage, nearby pressure or mitigations. A renewed infestation is entered
    as a new infested premises, so the chance of a renewed detection that the model then gives is
    lower than p in the first month or two (owners and inspection rounds must still find it), then about equal. The value cannot be tested until new months of data
    arrive. 0 when the option is off."""
    p = float(pack.get("renewed_chance", 0.0) or 0.0)
    if p <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return -math.log(1.0 - min(p, 0.999999)) / 30.0


def _read_intro_ref():
    """Factor on the reference introduction rate when the counties at risk are counted from the
    adjacency file, and the days per introduction it implies. Read from the linked-counties result
    (`event_scale` and `days_per_event_counted` in changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/results/
    index_reference.json, copied to data/): nine counted first detections in 3,576 county-days is one
    per 397 days, against the 130 days on record. None if the file is not there."""
    try:
        with open(_DATA / "index_reference.json") as f:
            ref = json.load(f)
        return float(ref["event_scale"]), float(ref["days_per_event_counted"])
    except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError):
        return None, None


INTRO_REF_FACTOR, INTRO_REF_DAYS = _read_intro_ref()


def _read_observed():
    """This year's monthly temperatures for the county (changes/2026-11-19-observed-weather/data/
    county_temperature_this_year.csv, copied to data/): twelve rows, January first. Months with
    observed days hold the 2026 values, adjusted from a station 21.5 km away; the rest hold the
    normals. None if the file is not there."""
    try:
        with open(_DATA / "county_temperature_this_year.csv", newline="") as f:
            rows = sorted(csv.DictReader(f), key=lambda r: int(r["month"]))
        if len(rows) != 12:
            return None
        return dict(
            year=2026,
            monthly_tmax=[float(r["tmax_c"]) for r in rows],
            monthly_tmin=[float(r["tmin_c"]) for r in rows],
            months=[int(r["month"]) for r in rows if int(r["days_observed"]) > 0],
            part_months=[int(r["month"]) for r in rows
                         if int(r["days_observed"]) > 0 and r["full_month"] != "yes"],
        )
    except (OSError, KeyError, ValueError):
        return None


COUNTY_OBSERVED = _read_observed()


def intro_ref_factor(pack: dict) -> float:
    """Multiplier on the reference introduction rate: 1 unless the pack asks for the adjacency count."""
    if pack.get("intro_ref", "record") == "adjacency" and INTRO_REF_FACTOR is not None:
        return INTRO_REF_FACTOR
    return 1.0


def module_schedule(pack: dict, horizon: float) -> dict:
    """The introduction module's schedule for a pack: what preset_to_params passes to the model and
    what the app draws, so the two cannot drift.

    With `weather_source="observed"` the segments that fall in an observed month of the observed
    year use this year's temperatures; every other segment keeps the normals. The run is taken to
    start in the observed year (the county's last detection was in June 2026), so a run longer than
    12 months returns to the normals in its second year. Each row carries `observed` (True or False)."""
    m = dict(pack, monthly_tmax=COUNTY["monthly_tmax"], monthly_tmin=COUNTY["monthly_tmin"])
    sc = _intro_schedule(m, horizon)
    for row in sc["rows"]:
        row["observed"] = False
    if pack.get("weather_source", "normals") != "observed" or COUNTY_OBSERVED is None:
        return sc
    mo = dict(pack, monthly_tmax=COUNTY_OBSERVED["monthly_tmax"],
              monthly_tmin=COUNTY_OBSERVED["monthly_tmin"])
    so = _intro_schedule(mo, horizon)
    start = int(pack["start_month"]) - 1
    for j in range(len(sc["schedule_times"])):
        k = start + j                               # months since January of the observed year
        if k < 12 and (k + 1) in COUNTY_OBSERVED["months"]:
            sc["intro_multiplier"][j] = so["intro_multiplier"][j]
            sc["spread_multiplier"][j] = so["spread_multiplier"][j]
            sc["rows"][j] = dict(so["rows"][j], observed=True)
    return sc

def rounds_in(pack: dict) -> int:
    """Number of inspection rounds in the period covered: floor(period_days / round_interval).
    A last partial round is dropped. A pack that still carries an explicit `n_rounds` keeps it."""
    if "n_rounds" in pack:
        return int(pack["n_rounds"])
    interval = float(pack["round_interval"])
    if interval <= 0.0:
        return 0
    return int(math.floor(float(pack["period_days"]) / interval + 1e-9))


def preset_to_params(pack: dict, dt: float) -> dict:
    """Map an app input pack to the lane's parameter dict. The ONLY such mapping."""
    n_rounds = rounds_in(pack)
    interval = float(pack["round_interval"])
    round_times = [round(interval * (i + 1), 6) for i in range(n_rounds)]
    horizon = max(round_times) if round_times else 0.0
    mean_recovery = float(pack["clearance_mean"]) if pack["clearance_on"] else math.inf
    recovery_within = (float(pack["mean_recovery_time_within"]) if pack["recovery_within_on"]
                       else math.inf)
    doubling_between = float(pack["doubling_time"]) if pack["spread_on"] else math.inf
    # 2026-10-24: a pack without the new keys (any pack written before them) keeps both switches off
    course_end = bool(pack.get("course_end_on", False))
    release = (float(pack["release_mean"]) if pack.get("release_on", False) else None)
    rate = float(pack["intro_rate"]) * intro_ref_factor(pack)    # factor 1 unless the option is on
    intro_interval = math.inf if rate <= 0.0 else 1.0 / rate
    sched = {}
    if pack.get("module_on", False) and horizon > 0.0:
        sc = module_schedule(pack, horizon)       # the normals, unless the weather option is on
        sched = dict(schedule_times=sc["schedule_times"], intro_multiplier=sc["intro_multiplier"],
                     spread_multiplier=sc["spread_multiplier"])
    # What-if term for renewed infestations (renewed_rate above). Nothing runs at 0, so every
    # parameter set is unchanged when the option is off. The schedule multiplies the reference rate,
    # so the constant rate h goes in as h / reference rate on every segment. With a reference rate
    # of zero the reference becomes h and the multipliers 1. With the module off, h is added to the
    # rate itself.
    h = renewed_rate(pack)
    if h > 0.0:
        if sched and rate > 0.0:
            sched["intro_multiplier"] = [a + h / rate for a in sched["intro_multiplier"]]
        elif sched:
            sched["intro_multiplier"] = [1.0 for _ in sched["intro_multiplier"]]
            intro_interval = 1.0 / h
        else:
            intro_interval = 1.0 / (rate + h)
    return dict(
        **sched,
        mean_latent_time=float(pack["mean_latent_time"]),
        doubling_time_within=float(pack["doubling_time_within"]),
        mean_recovery_time_within=recovery_within,
        N_herd=int(pack["N_herd"]),
        p_latent_seed=float(pack["p_latent_seed"]),
        p_infectious_seed=float(pack["p_infectious_seed"]),
        f_clinical_max=float(pack["f_clinical_max"]),
        mean_clinical_onset_time=float(pack["mean_clinical_onset_time"]),
        rho_a=float(pack["rho_a"]),
        rho_r=float(pack["rho_r"]),
        owner_contact_interval=float(pack.get("owner_contact_interval", 0.0)),   # issue #48
        Se_animal=float(pack["Se_animal"]),
        n_animals_per_round=int(pack["n_animals_per_round"]),
        mean_intro_interval=intro_interval,
        doubling_time=doubling_between,
        mean_recovery_time=mean_recovery,
        beta_lockdown_multiplier=float(pack["beta_lockdown_multiplier"]),
        course_end_exit=course_end,       # 2026-10-24 (accepted 2026-10-28)
        mean_release_time=release,        # 2026-10-24: None = the lane's single clearance rate
        design_prevalence=float(pack["design_prevalence"]),
        M=int(pack["M"]),
        round_times=round_times,
        n_farms_per_round=int(pack["n_farms_per_round"]),
        horizon=horizon,
        # initial state and the release floor (v0.6): the lane reads all three. Before today the
        # threshold stayed in the app, so the lane's t_release ran on its own default.
        k0_mean=float(pack["k0_mean"]),
        age0_scale=float(pack["age0_scale"]),
        release_threshold=float(pack["release_threshold"]),
        dt=float(dt),                     # inherited from the lane, never restated
        c_lost_freedom=float(pack["c_lost_freedom"] or 0.0),
        c_per_case=float(pack["c_per_case"] or 0.0),
        c_per_test=float(pack["c_per_test"] or 0.0),
        c_per_round=float(pack["c_per_round"] or 0.0),
    )

data/README.md
content:
# Data files read by the review app

Copies, unchanged, so that the browser build of the app (which ships this folder only) can read them.
Do not edit them here. Rebuild them at the source and copy again.

| File | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `detections_official.csv` | `changes/2026-11-18-county-tailoring/data/` | nearby-pressure index; last detection per county |
| `county_centroids_all.csv` | `changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/data/` | nearby-pressure index |
| `county_adjacency.csv` | `changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/data/` | reference level of the index |
| `index_reference.json` | `changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/results/` | factor for the introduction-rate option; counts on the 2026 tab |
| `linked_counties.csv`, `linked_group.csv`, `linked_summary.json` | `changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/results/` | "Neighbouring counties" tab |
| `backcheck_fair.json`, `backcheck_fair_seven.csv` | `changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/results/` (`backcheck_fair.json`; the seven in-group rows of `backcheck_fair.csv`) | "Check against 2026" tab and the caution under the county headline: the check on equal windows |
| `backcheck_group.csv`, `backcheck_texas.json` | `changes/2026-11-19-linked-counties/results/` | not read by the app since 18 November 2026; first version of the check, superseded |
| `calibration_2026_summary.json` | a few values taken from `fit.json` and `outcomes_summary.json` in `changes/2026-11-19-calibration-2026/results/` | "Check against 2026" tab; help text of the what-if input |
| `county_temperature_this_year.csv` | `changes/2026-11-19-observed-weather/data/` | "2026 observed" weather option |

Copied on 18 November 2026.
